traps.why: Methoxide (anionic) attacks the LESS substituted carbon by SN2. The more-substituted product is the acid-catalysed outcome.

explanation: Anionic nucleophiles open the strained ring by SN2 at the less substituted (less hindered) carbon, inverting it; the alkoxide is protonated by the solvent or the workup.
tip: Anionic nucleophile → less substituted carbon, inversion there.
